correctness.rationale: The Dirac-edge reduction uses optimal input/output couplings and graph geodesics. Cyclic mass-flow duality reduces neighbor-kernel W1 to a median absolute deviation, with the transport identity explicitly credited to prior work. A reflected heat difference system has an irreducible Metzler generator (odd end diagonal -3, even -4), proving strict radial monotonicity. Shell counting identifies the exact median. A nonnegative defect expansion and the combinatorial heat-kernel Taylor coefficients show all derivatives before k_N vanish and the first equals -a_N. Fourier decomposition proves the stated fixed-N tail. A separate numerical Kantorovich dual LP matches the formula in 140 instances, and exact integer matrix powers verify 589 Taylor identities; neither finite test substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: Sharp delay k_N=floor((N+2)/4) and the residue-class coefficient are exact spectral-transport invariants for every finite cycle, not a recomputation of a finite table. The increasing order of vanishing quantifies how graph circumference hides mixing from first-order curvature even though every positive time contracts, yielding sharp benchmarks across an infinite family. The all-time formula and analytic proof make the boundary reproducible and interpretable.
